actual: Nightly silent-degradation audit has no suppression mechanism; confirmed false positives such as SDA-2d2969408339 recur every night and require repeat human review. finding_id is unstable for LLM findings, so ad hoc finding_id-only suppression would be unreliable.
closure_requirements: Keep BUG JSON and GitHub Issue synchronized.
description:
Tool debt: scripts/nightly_silent_degradation_audit.py and configs/validation/silent_degradation_audit.yaml currently have no suppression/allowlist.

Current behavior:
- deterministic_findings() and _coerce_llm_findings() are merged into payload["findings"] in build_audit().
- workflow_gate is computed as warning when findings remain, otherwise ready.
- finding_id is SDA-sha256(module,title,reference_refs,code_refs)[:12]. LLM title/code_refs can drift nightly, so suppression must not rely only on finding_id.

Triggering confirmed false positive:
- SDA-2d2969408339 (P1, confidence 0.7, MiniQMT runtime lacks fail-closed) was Tier2-reviewed as false positive.
- runtime.py:845, client.py:822, and gateway.py:255 are per-order fail-closed-and-loud: explicit error_code + REJECTED/accepted=False + exception detail, not silent degradation.
- The finding recurs nightly and consumes human review.

Required design:
- Add optional top-level suppressions list to configs/validation/silent_degradation_audit.yaml.
- Each suppression has module, optional finding_id, optional code_refs_any path-prefix matching while ignoring line numbers, optional case-insensitive title_contains guard, reason, dismissed_by, dismissed_at YYYY-MM-DD, and optional expires_at YYYY-MM-DD.
- Missing suppressions keeps current behavior unchanged.
- A suppression matches only when module matches and either finding_id exact or code_refs_any overlaps finding.code_refs by path prefix, plus title_contains when present.
- A suppression with neither finding_id nor code_refs_any is config error and must raise SilentDegradationAuditError loudly.
- Expired suppressions are inactive.
- In build_audit(), apply suppressions after findings are aggregated and before workflow_gate calculation.
- Matched findings are removed from findings, appended to suppressed_findings with suppressed_by metadata, and do not trigger warning.
- public_artifact() must include suppressed_findings for auditability; suppressed findings must not be silently discarded.

First configured suppression:
- module: miniqmt_execution_runtime
- finding_id: SDA-2d2969408339
- code_refs_any: backend/services/miniqmt_execution_runtime/runtime.py, backend/services/miniqmt_execution_runtime/client.py, backend/services/miniqmt_execution_runtime/gateway.py
- title_contains: fail-closed
- reason: Tier2 manual review 2026-06-24: per-order fail-closed-and-loud (explicit error_code + REJECTED/accepted=False + exception detail); not silent degradation.
- dismissed_by: tier2-review
- dismissed_at: 2026-06-24
- expires_at: 2026-09-24

Acceptance tests:
1. Matching finding moves to suppressed_findings and is removed from findings; with no other findings workflow_gate is ready.
2. Nonmatching module or code_refs leaves finding in findings and workflow_gate warning.
3. Expired suppression is inactive and finding reappears.
4. SDA-2d29-like finding is suppressed by the YAML entry.
5. Suppression missing both finding_id and code_refs_any raises SilentDegradationAuditError.
6. public_artifact() includes suppressed_findings.
7. No suppressions section preserves current findings/workflow_gate behavior.
expected: Provide structured, auditable, expiring suppression. Suppressed findings remain visible in suppressed_findings and public artifacts, do not count toward workflow_gate, and invalid suppression config fails loudly.
non_goals: Do not restart production runtime services without explicit approval.
title: nightly silent-degradation audit lacks auditable suppression for confirmed false positives
